# BTS mega world tour sparks target-price upgrades for HYBE

## Brokerages lift price targets as massive world tour boosts earnings outlook

1

2026-01-18 06:59:07 

K-pop

The unveiling of a mega-scale world tour by BTS has prompted South Korean brokerages to raise their target prices for HYBE, reflecting growing confidence in a sharp earnings rebound this year.  
  
HYBE shares closed up 2.27% at 338,500 won on Friday, extending their one-month gain to 13.02%, according to the Korea Exchange. Over the same period, retail and foreign investors net bought 38.8 billion won and 11.1 billion won of the stock, respectively.  
  
While HYBE’s fourth-quarter results for last year are expected to fall short of market estimates, investors appear to be looking ahead to 2026, with optimism bolstered by the newly announced BTS tour schedule.  
  
BTS will launch what is set to be the largest world tour in K-pop history, spanning this year through the first half of next year. The tour will begin with three shows at Goyang Stadium on April 9, followed by performances in 35 cities across 23 countries, totaling 79 shows. Including potential additional dates next year, the number of concerts could exceed 85 – well above earlier market expectations of 65-70 shows.  
  
  
   
Attendance estimates have also been revised sharply higher. Total audience numbers this year are projected at around 4.5 million, with average attendance of roughly 65,000 per show, surpassing prior forecasts of 3.0 million to 3.5 million across about 65 concerts.  
  
The tour is expected to drive a marked improvement in HYBE’s financial performance. According to estimates compiled by FnGuide, HYBE’s revenue this year is forecast to jump 46.93% year on year to 3.87 trillion won, while operating profit is projected to surge 555.74% to 480 billion won.  
  
Following the tour announcement, brokerages moved swiftly to lift valuations. Kiwoom Securities raised its target price to 450,000 won from 380,000 won, while LS Securities increased its target to 430,000 won from 390,000 won. Yuanta Securities lifted its target to 420,000 won from 395,000 won, and IBK Investment & Securities raised its target to 420,000 won from 370,000 won.

content:
Getty Images for Gold House

In a same-day filing, Bang Si‑hyuk said he will donate 711,534 common shares — roughly 1.65% of outstanding stock — in a free transfer to HYBE and one other person. Based on February 12’s closing numbers, the donation package is worth about 270 billion KRW (or $186.8 million) intended to fund performance-based compensation for executives and employees.

HYBE will receive 546,120 shares as treasury stock while 165,414 shares will be donated to an unnamed individual outside the company. After the donations are complete, Bang’s stake would fall from 30.55% to 28.90%, still remaining the largest shareholder. HYBE said the chairman’s donation will secure the donated shares as treasury stock without separate expenditure. [...] Other projects teased for 2026 include the first full-length album from BOYNEXTDOOR, new music from LE SSERAFIM, a new girl group between HYBE and the U.S.-based label Geffen Records created from an upcoming TV series titled _WORLD SCOUT: THE FINAL PIECE._ A boy group with Ryan Tedder is also reportedly in the works with auditions taking place around the world.

HYBE’s stock is up over 13% to date.

HYBE shares slightly slipped on Thursday, February 12, in a particularly busy day for the Korean-entertainment conglomerate that included a court decision, financial report and donation from the Korean-entertainment conglomerate’s chairman.

HYBE stock closed at 380,500 Korean won (approximately $263.64) on the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI), down 2,500 KRW ($1.73) from Wednesday’s close of 383,000 KRW for a -0.65% move for the day.

A Verdict and a Promise to Appeal in HYBE vs. Min Hee-Jin
---------------------------------------------------------

Thursday morning began with a Seoul court ruling in favor of HYBE’s former CEO, Min Hee-jin, in a shareholders’ dispute over the termination of a contract. The decision requires HYBE to pay roughly 25.5 billion Korean won (about $17.7 million), plus legal expenses, to the former producer behind [NewJeans](https://www.forbes.com/profile/newjeans/) with the company quickly announcing its intention to appeal.

PROMOTED

Following the court’s decision in the morning on Thursday, HYBE shared its plans to review and appeal. “HYBE finds it unfortunate that its views were not fully reflected in the court’s decision,” a representative for the company’s Global Corporate PR said in an official statement. “The company will review the written ruling and proceed with further legal steps, including an appeal.”

HYBE’s 2025 Q4 and FY Reports Revealed
--------------------------------------

HYBE also released its fourth-quarter and fiscal-year 2025 results, which show the company growing its top line with a slightly different story when it comes to the bottom line.

Yet operating profit dropped to 49.9 billion KRW ($59.2 million) — down almost 73% year over year — and EBITDA fell 47% to 154 billion KRW ($106.7 million).

Concerts were an engine of growth in 2025, generating 763.9 billion KRW ($529.6 million), up around 69% YoY and nearly matching recorded-music revenues for the year, underscoring the agency's affinity for both live performances and recorded music. Merchandising and licensing were also a major highlight, jumping 35.8% YoY to 570.6 billion KRW ($401.4 million).

Previously, HYBE CEO Jason Jaesang Lee said he anticipated “profitability headwinds will largely clear by the fourth quarter, allowing for the full-scale improvement of our revenue structure starting in 2026.”

HYBE did deliver on Lee’s words, reversing course from a 42.2 billion KRW operating loss in Q3 to 4.6 billion KRW operating profit in Q4, as operating expenses fell 7.5% quarter over quarter.

HYBE Chairman Bang Si-Hyuk Donates Big
--------------------------------------

[![Image 3: Gold Gala 2024 - Program](https://imageio.forbes.com/specials-images/imageserve/698ea2df6aded928e0f8167b/Gold-Gala-2024---Program/0x0.jpg?format=jpg&crop=4999,3334,x0,y169,safe&width=144)](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jeffbenjamin)

Honoree Bang Si-hyuk accepts an award on stage during Gold Gala 2024 at The Music Center on May 11, 2024 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images for Gold House)

Getty Images for Gold House

In a same-day filing, [Bang Si‑hyuk](https://www.forbes.com/profile/bang-si-hyuk/) said he will donate 711,534 common shares — roughly 1.65% of outstanding stock — in a free transfer to HYBE and one other person. Based on February 12’s closing numbers, the donation package is worth about 270 billion KRW (or $186.8 million) intended to fund performance-based compensation for executives and employees.

HYBE will receive 546,120 shares as treasury stock while 165,414 shares will be donated to an unnamed individual outside the company. After the donations are complete, Bang’s stake would fall from 30.55% to 28.90%, still remaining the largest shareholder. HYBE said the chairman’s donation will secure the donated shares as treasury stock without separate expenditure.

Thursday’s modest stock dip could suggest investors saw the court ruling as a contained hit — a potential one-off payout and headline risk — rather than a massive existential blow. Still, a 25.5 billion KRW payout is less than one percent of HYBE’s 2.65 trillion KRW revenue, but a large figure relative to the company’s operating profit of 49.9 billion KRW.

That said, the decision puts cash outflow on the table, hands momentum to Min and her new ventures, and extends reputational uncertainty around such an influential K-pop player. But HYBE’s promise to appeal will temper any immediate accounting impact.

Beyond the headlines, 2026 is an incredibly important year for HYBE and its artists musically.

In the upcoming music release schedule, HYBE has its newest act. CORTIS will release the new song “Mention Me,” included on the upcoming [Stephen Curry](https://www.forbes.com/profile/stephen-curry/)–produced _GOAT_ movie soundtrack, on Friday, February 13.

On March 20, [BTS](https://www.forbes.com/profile/bts/) will release their long-awaited _ARIRANG_ album, which has reportedly generated millions in pre-orders, with the likes of [Ryan Tedder](https://www.forbes.com/profile/ryan-tedder/), [Jon Bellion](https://www.forbes.com/profile/jon-bellion/), Diplo, Max Martin and more involved.
